Q: Efficiently Migrating 40TB of BLOB Data from Oracle to a Scalable System A:

The --no-privileges ( or --no-acl ) option used during the restore tells pg_restore to skip all GRANT and REVOKE statements in the dump. It is the direct reason why the object-level privileges were not restored.

Backup command (no changes need)

pg_dump.exe --file "D:\backup.dump" --host "source-host" --port "5432" --username "user" --format=c --blobs --compress "0" "database-name"

Restore command (remove --no-privileges)

pg_restore.exe --host "target-host" --port "5432" --username "user" --dbname "database-name" --no-owner --disable-triggers --single-transation --verbose "D:\backup.dump"

Q: Extract News article content from stored .html pages A:

The other answers here point to good libraries (readability-lxml, newspaper, trafilatura, boilerpipe), which is the right call for production use. But since the question asks how to do this across arbitrary pages "relatively accurately", it's worth showing the actual technique those libraries are built on, because it's simpler than it looks and doesn't need regex at all.

The idea: text density, not tag names

You can't reliably find "the article" by tag name or class (<article>, .content, .post-body...) because every site names things differently. What is consistent across sites is that the real article text is a block with a lot of plain text and comparatively few links, while navigation/sidebars/footers are the opposite: mostly short link text.

So: strip anything that's never article content, score every remaining block by "how much real text vs. link text it holds", and take the highest-scoring one.

python
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

BLOCK_TAGS = ("p", "article", "section", "div", "main")

def text_density(tag):
    text = tag.get_text(" ", strip=True)
    text_len = len(text)
    if text_len == 0:
        return 0.0
    link_text_len = sum(len(a.get_text(strip=True)) for a in tag.find_all("a"))
    link_ratio = link_text_len / text_len
    # long blocks score high, but get penalized the more of their
    # text sits inside <a> tags (nav/link-list blocks score low)
    return text_len * (1 - link_ratio)

def extract_main_content(html: str) -> str:
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")

    # drop stuff that's never the article body
    for tag in soup(["script", "style", "nav", "header", "footer", "aside", "form"]):
        tag.decompose()

    candidates = soup.find_all(BLOCK_TAGS)
    if not candidates:
        return soup.get_text(" ", strip=True)

    best = max(candidates, key=text_density)
    return best.get_text("\n", strip=True)

Usage:

with open("article.html", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    html = f.read()

print(extract_main_content(html))

I tested this against a real Dev.to article page (full of nav/sidebar/comments boilerplate) and it correctly pulled out just the article body, no false matches from the sidebar.

Where this breaks down (and what the real libraries add)

This single-heuristic version is a good teaching example but will misfire on some layouts:

  • Multi-paragraph articles split across many small <p> tags with no single wrapping container that scores highest — fix: score the best contiguous run of siblings, not a single tag.
  • Image-heavy articles where the real "highest text density" block is a caption or pull-quote, not the article — fix: add a minimum length floor before a candidate is even considered.
  • Comment sections, which are also text with a low link ratio — fix: explicitly exclude known comment-container patterns, or weight blocks lower the deeper they are in the DOM.

This is exactly the rabbit hole readability-lxml/trafilatura/boilerpipe have already gone down for you, combining this text/link-density signal with a dozen others (tag semantics, punctuation density, DOM depth, etc.) — so for production use, reach for one of those rather than hand-rolling it further. If you want it as a managed HTTP call instead of a library dependency (e.g. calling it from a non-Python service), Web Metadata Extractor exposes the same kind of extraction as a markdown endpoint that returns cleaned Markdown for a given URL — but the snippet above is the actual mechanism underneath this whole category of tool.

Q: How can I exclude holidays using my custom holiday table in my SQL code that excludes weekends A:

The following steps show how we can approach it step by step.

Prepare test data

CREATE TABLE dbo.Contacts(
    ContactID   INT        NOT NULL,
    ContactType VARCHAR(8) NOT NULL,
    ContactDate DATE       NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE dbo.Holidays(
    HolidayDesc VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    HolidayDate DATE        NOT NULL
);
GO
INSERT dbo.Contacts(ContactID, ContactType, ContactDate)
VALUES (12345, 'TYPE1', '6/18/2026'),
       (12345, 'TYPE2', '6/25/2026'),
       (67890, 'TYPE1', '6/18/2026'),
       (67890, 'TYPE2', '6/24/2026');
INSERT dbo.Holidays(HolidayDesc, HolidayDate)
VALUES ('Juneteenth', '6/19/2026'),
       ('Independence Day', '7/3/2026');

List the dates from the date of TYPE1 to the date of TYPE2

SELECT c1.ContactID,
       DATEADD(DAY, v.number, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
FROM   dbo.Contacts       AS c1
JOIN   dbo.Contacts       AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
JOIN   master..spt_values AS v  ON v.type = 'P'
   AND v.number BETWEEN 1 AND DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1';

Output:

ContactID   Date
----------- ----------
12345       2026-06-19
12345       2026-06-20
12345       2026-06-21
12345       2026-06-22
12345       2026-06-23
12345       2026-06-24
12345       2026-06-25
67890       2026-06-19
67890       2026-06-20
67890       2026-06-21
67890       2026-06-22
67890       2026-06-23
67890       2026-06-24

Here we can leverage the system table master..spt_values which comes with various sequences of convenient numbers. When type column equals 'P', the value of number column would be a sequence from 0 to 2047. Using the numbers to add dates can give us a range of 5.6 years, should be more than enough.

See also: Using a Table of Numbers

Note that we skip the starting date of the same ContactID group for ease of counting the dates in the following steps.

Count working days

WITH Dates AS (
    SELECT c1.ContactID,
           DATEADD(DAY, v.number, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
    FROM   dbo.Contacts       AS c1
    JOIN   dbo.Contacts       AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
    JOIN   master..spt_values AS v  ON v.type = 'P'
       AND v.number BETWEEN 1 AND DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
    WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
)
SELECT d.ContactID,
       COUNT(*) AS CountWorkDays
FROM   Dates AS d
WHERE  DATENAME(WEEKDAY, d.Date) NOT IN ('Saturday','Sunday')
   AND NOT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1
       FROM   dbo.Holidays AS h
       WHERE  h.HolidayDate = d.Date
   )
GROUP  BY d.ContactID;

Output:

ContactID   CountWorkDays
----------- -------------
12345       4
67890       3

Use the last result as a CTE to generate 'Yes' / 'No' result

WITH Dates AS (
    SELECT c1.ContactID,
           DATEADD(DAY, v.number, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
    FROM   dbo.Contacts       AS c1
    JOIN   dbo.Contacts       AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
    JOIN   master..spt_values AS v  ON v.type = 'P'
       AND v.number BETWEEN 1 AND DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
    WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
),
WorkDaysCount AS (
    SELECT d.ContactID,
           COUNT(*) AS CountWorkDays
    FROM   Dates AS d
    WHERE  DATENAME(WEEKDAY, d.Date) NOT IN ('Saturday','Sunday')
       AND NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM   dbo.Holidays AS h
           WHERE  h.HolidayDate = d.Date
       )
    GROUP  BY d.ContactID
)
SELECT c.ContactID,
       c.ContactType,
       c.ContactDate,
       CASE WHEN w.CountWorkDays <= 3 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Day3Validate
FROM   dbo.Contacts AS c
JOIN   WorkDaysCount AS w ON c.ContactID = w.ContactID
WHERE  c.ContactType = 'TYPE2';

Output:

ContactID   ContactType ContactDate Day3Validate
----------- ----------- ----------- ------------
12345       TYPE2       2026-06-25  No
67890       TYPE2       2026-06-24  Yes

Get rid of undocumented feature

Using the undocumented master..spt_values system table could be a problem if in the future it is removed from a new release of SQL Server. It's also not supported by other RDBMS. Starting from SQL Server 2022 a new table-value function GENERATE_SERIES(start, stop [, step ]) can be used, which is also more flexible. In the following example query the numbers range from 1 to 10,000, should be enough to support 27 years of data.

WITH Dates AS (
    SELECT c1.ContactID,
           DATEADD(DAY, n.value, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
    FROM   dbo.Contacts              AS c1
    JOIN   dbo.Contacts              AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
    JOIN   GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10000) AS n  ON n.value <= DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
    WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
),
WorkDaysCount AS (
    SELECT d.ContactID,
           COUNT(*) AS CountWorkDays
    FROM   Dates AS d
    WHERE  DATENAME(WEEKDAY, d.Date) NOT IN ('Saturday','Sunday')
       AND NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM   dbo.Holidays AS h
           WHERE  h.HolidayDate = d.Date
       )
    GROUP  BY d.ContactID
)
SELECT c.ContactID,
       c.ContactType,
       c.ContactDate,
       CASE WHEN w.CountWorkDays <= 3 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Day3Validate
FROM dbo.Contacts  AS c
JOIN WorkDaysCount AS w ON c.ContactID = w.ContactID
WHERE c.ContactType = 'TYPE2';

A more portable solution

GENERATE_SERIES() is only available in SQL Server. To write a more portable query, we need to generate a number series on-the-fly.

WITH T1(F) AS (
    SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL 
    SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL 
    SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1
),                      
T2(F) AS (SELECT 1 FROM T1 AS A, T1 AS B),
T3(F) AS (SELECT 1 FROM T2 AS A, T2 AS B),
T4(F) AS (SELECT 1 FROM T3 AS A, T3 AS B),
Numbers(value) AS (
    SELECT TOP(10000) ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL))
    FROM   T4
),
Dates AS (
    SELECT c1.ContactID,
           DATEADD(DAY, n.value, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
    FROM   dbo.Contacts AS c1
    JOIN   dbo.Contacts AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
    JOIN   Numbers      AS n  ON n.value <= DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
    WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
),
WorkDaysCount AS (
    SELECT d.ContactID,
           COUNT(*) AS CountWorkDays
    FROM   Dates AS d
    WHERE  DATENAME(WEEKDAY, d.Date) NOT IN ('Saturday','Sunday')
       AND NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM   dbo.Holidays AS h
           WHERE  h.HolidayDate = d.Date
       )
    GROUP  BY d.ContactID
)
SELECT c.ContactID,
       c.ContactType,
       c.ContactDate,
       CASE WHEN w.CountWorkDays <= 3 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Day3Validate
FROM dbo.Contacts  AS c
JOIN WorkDaysCount AS w ON c.ContactID = w.ContactID
WHERE c.ContactType = 'TYPE2';

The technique is documented in: Generate N sequential numbers (fast) - SQLServerCentral

Q: How to avoid codeigniter skipping empty URL parameters A:

to prevent missing parameter issues you should use the following code

make your routes like below

$route['(.*)'] = 'controller/method';

.* => it will return all parametar after the method

update your function as below

public function () {
    $controller = $this->uri->segment(1); // controller
    $method = $this->uri->segment(2); // method
    $param1 = $this->uri->segment(3); // p1
    $param2 = $this->uri->segment(4); // p2
    $param3 = $this->uri->segment(5); // p3
}

Q: What is routes/index.js and its purpose? A:

In login.js, you can define your routes and to make these routes work, you need to import this file to your index.js.

So in this way if you are working on a large scale project, you can just follow this modular approach and define routes in different files and include all these files in index.js file.
